question: Who was the founder of the Khudai Khidmatgars?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, **also known as "Frontier Gandhi," was the founder of the *Khudai Khidmatgars*, or "Servants of God.**"
 
• This **movement was a non-violent resistance organization formed in the North-West Frontier Province** (present-day Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan) to fight British colonial rule.
 
• **Ghaffar Khan was a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi** and a prominent advocate of non-violence.
 
• The Khudai Khidmatgars promoted peace, social reform, and independence from British rule, relying on peaceful protests and social activism rather than armed struggle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sayyid Ahmed Khan:**

 
 
• He was a prominent 19th-century Muslim scholar and reformer in British India, known for founding the Aligarh Movement and Aligarh Muslim University to promote modern education among Muslims. 
 
 
 
• **Maulana Azad:**
 
 
• Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was a senior leader in the Indian independence movement and the first Education Minister of independent India. 
 
 
 
• **Mohammad Ali Jinnah**:
 
 
• Jinnah was the leader of the All India Muslim League and later the founder of Pakistan.
 
• He played a significant role in the political landscape of British India but was not involved with the Khudai Khidmatgars movement.
